'''Emmanuel Kabeya Mudiay''' (born March 5, 1996) is a Congolese-American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN). He played high school basketball for [[Grace Preparatory Academy]] and [[Prime Prep Academy]] in [[Texas]], where he received media attention. He committed to play for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball]] team on August 24, 2013, but later made the decision to forgo college and joined the [[Guangdong Southern Tigers]] in China. After an injury-riddled season in China, he was selected with the seventh overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Denver Nuggets]].

==Early life==
Mudiay was born on March 5, 1996, in [[Kinshasa]], [[Zaire]] (now the [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]) to Jean-Paul Mudiay and Therese Kabeya. His father died when he was a toddler, and the family was tremendously troubled by the [[Second Congo War]]. He lived under the constant threat of the instability in the region, while his mother grew only enough coffee and vegetables to support their needs. In 2001, Kabeya and her sons sought asylum in the United States and eventually escaped.<ref name=dallasnews>{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Once endangered by African war, SMU signee Emmanuel Mudiay aims for NBA career|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/smu-mustangs/20140308-once-endangered-by-african-war-smu-signee-emmanuel-mudiay-aims-for-nba-career.ece|work=DallasNews.com|date=March 8, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924121828/http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/college-sports/smu-mustangs/20140308-once-endangered-by-african-war-smu-signee-emmanuel-mudiay-aims-for-nba-career.ece|url-status=dead}}</ref> He primarily spoke [[French language|French]] upon arriving in the United States, but his older brother said, "We felt like Americans."<ref name="dallasnews" />

==High school career==
[[File:20140402 MCDAAG Emmanuel Mudiay tomahawk dunk (2).JPG|thumb|Mudiay at the [[2014 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]]]]
In his freshman season, Mudiay attended [[Grace Preparatory Academy]] in [[Arlington, Texas]], where he played alongside [[Isaiah Austin]], who became an elite college [[Center (basketball)|center]] before being diagnosed with [[Marfan syndrome]]. Mudiay scored 16 points in the 2011 [[Texas Association of Private and Parochial Schools|TAPPS]] Class 4A Final, helping the team defeat two-time champions [[Westbury Christian School]] with the score of 42–37.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Smith|first1=Corbett|title=Basketball Player of the Year: Emmanuel Mudiay's rise has next stop at SMU|url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/high-schools/boys-basketball-news/headlines/20140320-boys-poy.ece|work=DallasNews.com|date=March 20, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014|archive-date=September 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924125621/http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/high-schools/boys-basketball-news/headlines/20140320-boys-poy.ece|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mudiay transferred to [[Prime Prep Academy]] in [[Dallas, Texas]], with head coach Ray Forsett for his final seasons in high school. The program was put under scrutiny following the ineligibility of Karviar Sheperd and [[Jordan Mickey]], two elite collegiate prospects. Upon excellent seasons with Prime Prep, however, Mudiay was rated the second-best recruit in his class by [[Rivals.com]]. He was also touted as a possible [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|number one]] pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Payne|first1=Terrence|title=Top-5 recruit Emmanuel Mudiay will return to Prime Prep|url=https://collegebasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/07/23/top-5-recruit-emmanuel-mudiay-will-return-to-prime-prep/|work=NBCSports.com|date=July 23, 2013|access-date=July 15, 2014}}</ref>

He committed to play for the [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball]] team on August 24, 2013, because of the prospect of being coached by [[Larry Brown (basketball)|Larry Brown]], who previously won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA title]] with the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>[http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/23302984/smu-makes-statement-with-emmanuel-mudiays-commitment SMU makes statement with Emmanuel Mudiay's commitment]</ref> Mudiay selected the school over other possibilities with the likes of [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]], [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Emmanuel Mudiay|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Emmanuel-Mudiay-120454|work=Yahoo.com|access-date=July 15, 2014}}</ref>

In the summer of 2014, Mudiay made the decision to forgo college and play overseas after considering playing in the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. The move drew comparisons with [[Brandon Jennings]], who made a similar choice.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Gleeson|first1=Scott|title=Emmanuel Mudiay decides not to attend SMU, will turn pro overseas|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2014/07/14/emmanuel-mudiay-smu-decides-to-turn-pro-overseas/12634877/|work=USAToday.com|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last1=Thompson|first1=Tyler|title=Emmanuel Mudiay releases a statement|url=https://kentuckysportsradio.com/basketball-2/emmanuel-mudiay-releases-a-statement/|work=KentuckySportsRadio.com|date=July 14, 2014|access-date=July 15, 2014}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2018–2019)===
On February 8, 2018, Mudiay was acquired by the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Devin Harris]] and a second-round pick, as part of a three-team trade with the Nuggets and the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks acquire Emmanual Mudiay in 3-team trade|url=https://www.nba.com/article/2018/02/08/new-york-knicks-acquire-emmanual-mudiay-three-team-deal-official-release#/|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> In his debut for the Knicks three days later, Mudiay had 14 points and 10 assists in a 121–113 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jonah|last=Ballow|title=IND 121, NYK 113: Three Knicks Register Double-Double Performances in Indy|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/post-game-report-presented-major-energy/ind-121-nyk-113-three-knicks-register-double-double|work=NBA.com|date=February 12, 2018|access-date=February 12, 2018}}</ref>

Two days prior to the start of the 2018–19 season, Mudiay sprained his right ankle in practice; an injury which would sideline him for over two weeks.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tommy|last=Beer|title=Emmanuel Mudiay Is Rewarding Knicks Coach Fizdale's Faith|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/tommybeer/2018/11/27/emmanuel-mudiay-rewarding-coach-fizdales-faith/|work=Forbes.com|date=November 27, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2018}}</ref> On December 14, he scored a career-high 34 points in a 126–124 overtime win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mudiay scores 34, short-handed Knicks beat Hornets in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071102|work=ESPN.com|date=December 14, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Stefan|last=Bondy|title=Emmanuel Mudiay's career night helps Knicks stage frenzied comeback to beat Hornets in OT|url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/knicks/ny-sports-knicks-hornets-20181214-story.html|work=NYDailyNews.com|date=December 14, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2018}}</ref> On January 25, he was diagnosed with a left shoulder strain and was ruled out for at least two weeks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks' Emmanuel Mudiay: Out for at least two weeks|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-emmanuel-mudiay-out-for-at-least-two-weeks/|work=CBSSports.com|date=January 25, 2019|access-date=January 25, 2019}}</ref> He returned from a 12-game absence on February 22 against the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Wolves overcome Towns' first absence, beat Knicks 115-104|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071551|work=ESPN.com|date=February 22, 2019|access-date=February 22, 2019}}</ref> Mudiay missed the final two games of the season because of a sore left shoulder.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks top Bulls 96-86, avoid new franchise low for wins|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071886|work=ESPN.com|date=April 9, 2019|access-date=April 10, 2019}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2019–2020)===
On July 20, 2019, Mudiay signed with the [[Utah Jazz]]. In an interview shortly after signing with the Jazz, he was asked specifically why he chose to sign with the Jazz organization and he stated that he "can look at him [<nowiki/>[[Mike Conley Jr.|Mike Conley]]] like a big brother and he can mentor me" and "a lot of players that have come here have developed and gotten better and that's something that I wanted to do." He also stated he had never played in the playoffs and that's something that he wanted to do.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz Sign Ed Davis, Jeff Green and Emmanuel Mudiay|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/jazz-sign-davis-green-and-mudiay|website=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2019|access-date=July 20, 2019}}</ref>

===Žalgiris Kaunas (2021)===
On August 23, 2021, Mudiay officially signed a one-year deal with Lithuanian club [[BC Žalgiris|Žalgiris Kaunas]] of the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro |title=Emmanuel Mudiay set to join Zalgiris Kaunas|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/emmanuel-mudiay-set-to-join-zalgiris-kaunas/|website=Sportando.basketball|date=August 24, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}}</ref>

On November 2, 2021, Mudiay and Žalgiris mutually parted ways.<ref>{{cite web|title=Tai Webster replaces Emmanuel Mudiay in Zalgiris|url=https://zalgiris.lt/en/news/bc-zalgiris/97831/|website=Zalgiris.lt|date=November 2, 2021|access-date=November 2, 2021}}</ref> Mudiay averaged 7.4 points, 3.2 assists and 2.2 rebounds while shooting 32.5% from the field over 5 games with the club.

===Sacramento Kings (2021–2022)===
On December 22, 2021, Mudiay signed a 10-day contract with the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kings Sign Emmanuel Mudiay|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-emmanuel-mudiay|website=NBA.com|date=December 22, 2021|access-date=December 22, 2021}}</ref>

===Iowa Wolves (2022–2023)===
On November 2, 2022, Mudiay was named to the opening night roster for the [[Iowa Wolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/iowa-wolves-finalize-opening-night-roster/n-5895237|title=Iowa Wolves Finalize Opening Night Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=November 2, 2022|access-date=November 2, 2022}}</ref>

===Cangrejeros de Santurce (2023)===
On June 8, 2023, Mudiay signed with [[Cangrejeros de Santurce (basketball)|Cangrejeros de Santurce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican league]].<ref>{{cite tweet|number=1666883155826024448|title=OFICIAL: El armador ex-NBA Emmanuel Mudiay es el nuevo refuerzo de los Cangrejeros de Santurce hasta la recuperación de Davis Stockton.|user=LaGuerraBSN|author=La Guerra del BSN|date=June 8, 2023|access-date=June 8, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref>

===Piratas de Quebradillas (2024–present)===
On February 13, 2024, Mudiay signed with the [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tacko Fall and Emmanuel Mudiay sign with a team in Puerto Rico|url=https://m.basketnews.com/news-201859-tacko-fall-and-emmanuel-mudiay-sign-with-a-team-in-puerto-rico.html|access-date=February 16, 2024|website=basketnews.com|language=en}}</ref>

On June 13, 2024, Mudiay was drafted by the [[Valley Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA G League expansion draft]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2024-25 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2024-expansion-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2024|access-date=June 14, 2024}}</ref>

On July 1, 2025, Mudiay was named the 2025 [[BSN Most Valuable Player Award|BSN Most Valuable Player]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Reboyras |first1=Joseph |title=Emmanuel Mudiay gana el MVP e Iván "Pipo" Vélez se lleva el Dirigente del Año en los BSN Awards |url=https://www.primerahora.com/deportes/baloncesto/notas/emmanuel-mudiay-gana-el-mvp-e-ivan-pipo-velez-se-lleva-el-dirigente-del-ano-en-los-bsn-awards/ |website=primerahora.com |publisher=Primera Hora |access-date=1 July 2025}}</ref>

==National team career==
During the 2016 off-season, Mudiay was part of the USA Men's Select Team, a team selected to train with the USA Basketball Men's National Team in preparation for the 2016 Rio Summer Olympics.<ref>{{cite web |last=Huang |first=Jonathan |date=June 7, 2016 |title=USA Basketball Names 2016 Men's Select Team |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-2016-men%27s-select-team-060716 |access-date=June 14, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>
